Using DataEditR in Shiny apps

Source: vignettes/shiny-modules.Rmd
shiny-modules.Rmd

data_edit() is a shiny gadget built from a set of shiny modules. The same modules can be used to add an editable table to your own shiny applications. This article shows how to use the dataEdit module and how it fits together with the other modules that ship with DataEditR.

1. The dataEdit module

Every shiny module has two parts: a user interface function to place in the UI of your app, and a server function to call in your server. For the data editor these are dataEditUI() and dataEditServer(). Give both the same id:

library(shiny)
library(DataEditR)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Car data"),
  dataEditUI("cars")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  cars <- dataEditServer("cars", data = reactive(mtcars))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

dataEditUI() adds the grid together with the toolbar (undo/redo, columns, find, review changes, code and keyboard shortcuts), the review panel and the status bar. The grid supports everything described in vignette("DataEditR"): editing, range selection, copy and paste, fill down, adding and removing rows and columns, header filters, change tracking and the review panel.

The editor uses Bootstrap 5, so use a Bootstrap 5 page such as bslib::page_fluid() (or fluidPage(theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 5))) for the menus and dialogs to look their best.

1.1 Layout options

  • height sets the height of the grid ("65vh" by default);
  • toolbar = FALSE shows only the grid, without the toolbar, review panel and status bar;
  • toolbar_left and toolbar_right add your own controls at the start or end of the toolbar. data_edit() uses these slots for its Open and Export menus.
ui <- bslib::page_fluid(
  dataEditUI(
    "cars",
    height = "500px",
    toolbar_right = downloadButton("save", "Save", class = "btn-sm")
  )
)

1.2 Server options

dataEditServer() accepts the same editing options as data_edit(), including col_bind, col_edit, col_options, col_stretch, col_names, col_readonly, col_hide, col_factor, row_bind, row_edit, read_fun, read_args, quiet and track. The data argument can be a reactive expression or a fixed value, and can contain:

  • a data.frame, tibble, data.table or matrix;
  • the dimensions (e.g. c(10, 5)) or column names of an empty template;
  • the name of a file to read with read_fun;
  • a dbplyr lazy table or db_table() (see vignette("databases")).

Whenever data changes the editor loads the new data and its history is cleared. code_name sets the name of the data in the code shown in the Code tab.

1.3 The returned data

dataEditServer() returns a reactive expression containing the edited data, which updates after every change. Use it like any other reactive:

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  cars <- dataEditServer("cars", data = reactive(mtcars), track = TRUE)

  output$save <- downloadHandler(
    filename = "cars.csv",
    content = function(file) write.csv(cars(), file)
  )
}

The reactive also carries two attributes:

  • attr(cars, "view") is a reactive returning only the rows and columns on screen (after header filters, hidden columns and the rows/columns arguments below);
  • attr(cars, "editor") is a reactive returning the internal state of the editor (used by data_edit() to commit database changes).

1.4 Showing part of the data

The rows and columns arguments restrict what the grid shows without removing anything from the data. They accept fixed values or reactive expressions returning the row indices and column names to display (NULL shows everything). Edits made to the visible part are applied directly to the complete data, which is what the returned reactive contains.

ui <- bslib::page_fluid(
  checkboxGroupInput("cyl", "Cylinders", choices = c(4, 6, 8),
                     selected = c(4, 6, 8), inline = TRUE),
  dataEditUI("cars")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  cars <- dataEditServer(
    "cars",
    data = reactive(mtcars),
    rows = reactive(which(mtcars$cyl %in% input$cyl)),
    columns = c("mpg", "cyl", "hp", "wt")
  )
}

2. The other modules

Earlier versions of DataEditR combined several modules inside data_edit(). These are still exported and can be combined with dataEdit in your own apps. They use shinyjs, so add shinyjs::useShinyjs() to your UI.

Module What it does
dataInput text box to load an R object or template by name, and a file upload
dataOutput download button that writes the data to a file with any writing function
dataFilter dialog to build row filters (equal, greater than, between, contains, …)
dataSelect dialog to choose columns
dataSync merges an edited subset back into the complete data

dataFilterServer() returns a list with the filtered data and the matching rows, and dataSelectServer() a list with the selected data, column indices (columns) and column names. These can be passed straight to the rows and columns arguments of dataEditServer(), so there is no need for dataSync:

library(shiny)
library(shinyjs)
library(DataEditR)

ui <- bslib::page_fluid(
  useShinyjs(),
  dataInputUI("input"),
  dataFilterUI("filter"),
  dataSelectUI("select"),
  dataOutputUI("output"),
  dataEditUI("edit")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  data_input <- dataInputServer("input", data = "mtcars")
  data_filter <- dataFilterServer("filter", data = data_input)
  data_select <- dataSelectServer("select", data = data_input)

  data_edit <- dataEditServer(
    "edit",
    data = data_input,
    rows = data_filter$rows,
    columns = data_select$names
  )

  dataOutputServer("output", data = data_edit)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

By default dataFilterServer() and dataSelectServer() reset whenever their data changes. Supply a different trigger to reset (e.g. the data input rather than the edited data) to keep filters active while the data is being edited.

dataSyncServer() is still available for apps that edit a copy of a subset: give it the complete data, the edited data_subset and the rows and columns of the subset, and set auto = TRUE to merge changes as they happen.
